n1: Which model should do which job? Strong models are slow and costly on grind work, and fast models are careless on judgment calls. In a workflow you don't have to pick one. Each node pins its own model by class, fast, balanced, or deep, and Keelson resolves that class to a real model from your provider's catalog.
n2: Here a fast model maps the repo, a deep one plans a change, and a balanced one reviews the plan.
n3: Three phases, three models, one run.
n4: The run records which model really answered each node. Haiku explored, Opus planned, and Sonnet reviewed, and called the plan sound.
n5: They can be swapped because no node reads another's conversation. Each one writes its conclusions to a markdown file in the run's folder, and the next node opens that file with a fresh context. The file is the contract, so any phase can change models without the others noticing.
n6: So try a different reviewer. One line: replace balanced with a model from another vendor.
n8: Same graph, same handoff. This reviewer, GPT-6 Luna, reads it differently, calls the plan unsound, and names the step it would fix.
